bib.title: Nougat: Neural Optical Understanding for Academic Documents

question: Can an end-to-end image-to-markup transformer convert scientific document page images (including math and tables) into a lightweight markup language without any OCR engine or embedded text?
hypothesis: An OCR-free Donut-style encoder-decoder trained on page images paired with LaTeX-derived markup will beat PDF-embedded text and GROBID, especially on math, because those lose the semantic information of mathematical expressions.
contributions: Release of a pre-trained model capable of converting a PDF to a lightweight markup language (code and model on GitHub)
A pipeline to create a dataset pairing PDFs to source code
The method depends only on the image of a page, allowing access to scanned papers and books

method.summary: Nougat is a Donut-style encoder-decoder: a Swin-base encoder reads a rasterised page (896x672) and an mBART-style decoder emits markdown autoregressively. It is trained on a corpus of over eight million page/markup pairs built mostly from arXiv LaTeX (via LaTeXML) with PMC and IDL added for pre-training, with image augmentation and token-perturbation against repetition loops.
method.task: page image to markup (OCR for academic documents)

datasets.name: arXiv
datasets.source: arXiv open-access LaTeX source and compiled PDFs
datasets.preprocessing: LaTeXML to HTML5, then parsed to lightweight markdown; pages split via TF-IDF bag-of-words SVM plus Gini-impurity boundary search and fuzzy matching; pages kept only if average score >= 0.9 for both page breaks (about 47% acceptance); figures/tables removed with pdffigures2 and reinserted at page end

datasets.name: PMC
datasets.source: PubMed Central open access non-commercial subset, XML parsed to the same markup
datasets.preprocessing: display math and tables often images and ignored

datasets.name: IDL
datasets.source: Industry Documents Library with OCR text from Biten et al. (OCR-IDL)
datasets.preprocessing: OCR text only, no formatting; teaches basic OCR of scanned documents

models.name: Nougat base
models.architecture: Swin base encoder + mBART decoder with cross-attention, 10 decoder layers
models.tokenizer: same tokenizer as Galactica (Taylor et al.)

models.name: Nougat small
models.init_from: pre-trained base model (as stated: 'we start from the pre-trained base model')

models.name: GROBID (+ LaTeX-OCR for formulas)
models.architecture: rule/ML parser to XML converted to markup; formula boxes sent to LaTeX-OCR (pix2tex)

training.objective: inferred: autoregressive next-token cross-entropy on markup tokens (not stated explicitly)
training.lr_schedule: multiplied by 0.9996 every 15 updates until lr_end
training.regularisation: image augmentation (erosion, dilation, gaussian noise, gaussian blur, bitmap, image compression, grid distortion, elastic transform; fixed probability each; Albumentations); random token replacement in ground truth, repeated until a sampled number exceeds a 10% threshold

other.lr_note: low lr chosen 'due to training instabilities'

inference.samples: inferred: one greedy output per page; no repeats or seeds reported

parameters.repetition_threshold: 6.75 on VarEnd (post-hoc); online: last 200 tokens and half the threshold

other.speed: NVIDIA A10G 24GB, 6 pages in parallel, mean 19.5 s per batch, avg about 1400 tokens/page, base model, no inference optimisation

metrics.name: Edit distance
metrics.definition: normalised Levenshtein distance (character insertions, deletions, substitutions divided by total characters)

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: n-gram match between candidate and reference

metrics.name: Precision/Recall/F1
metrics.definition: F-measure with precision and recall reported (token level not specified)

eval.protocol: Single run on the arXiv test set (size not stated), split by modality (plain text, math, tables) and 'All'; no seeds, no significance tests; GROBID XML converted to the same markup with Unicode symbols mapped to LaTeX. Test-set page count not stated.

availability.data: dataset-generation pipeline code released; the dataset itself is not stated as released

limits: Repetition loops are the primary unsolved problem; the model cannot recover once it collapses, and 1.5% is for in-domain test pages only (5.4, 5.5).
Almost entirely English training data; non-Latin scripts produce instant repetitions; accented characters are replaced by closest Latin letter (5.5).
Slow: 19.5 s per 6-page batch on an A10G versus GROBID 10.6 PDF/s (5.5).
Trained page by page, so bibliography styles and section numbering are inconsistent across pages and numbers can be hallucinated (5.5).

Ground truth is noisy (LaTeXML artifacts, imperfect page splits, PMC math as images); LaTeX has many equivalent spellings, so math and plain-text scores are depressed even for visually identical output (4.2, 5.2).

Evaluation is only on the arXiv test set whose size is not stated; no scanned-document metrics, only qualitative examples (Appendix B), which are admitted to be noticeably worse than digital-born pages.
GROBID baseline was modified by the authors (Unicode-to-LaTeX mapping, LaTeX-OCR add-on) and its math scores are affected by bounding-box quality.
Training hardware, compute, warmup, precision, weight decay, dropout, seeds and test-set size are not stated.

code.snippet: VarWinB[l](x) = 1/B sum_{i=x}^{x+B} (l_i - 1/B sum_{j=x}^{x+B} l_j)^2 ; VarEndB[l](x) = variance of VarWinB from x to S; flag repetition if VarEnd drops below 6.75 and stays below (B = 15)

problems: Text cache contains foreign text (Sorscher data-pruning equations, VQA and WritingPrompts tables, calculus and NASA pages) because the PDF figures (Fig 5, B.1-B.4) embed page images with text layers; none of it is the paper's own content and none was used. No instructions found in it.
Section map labels (e.g. 'Method', Table 1/2/3/4) beyond Table 1 and A.1 belong to those embedded pages.
Hyperparameters like hidden size/heads/precision are not stated. Venue 'ICLR 2024' in the repo note is not in this PDF (arXiv v1).
